I hope that it has been going well for you so far. I finished a 30-day water fast a couple of weeks ago, and though I didn't have any trouble with strength during that time, I must admit that I was not often engaged in strenuous activity.

I've read that around day 9-11 of water fasting is when your body really gets into the swing of things (something about ketones) , any anecdotes about this?

I don't know what you mean by "gets into the swing of things." Could you clarify?

As for ketones, they begin production after about 3 or 4 days of fasting, or before that if you were eating low-carb beforehand. Ketones are molecules that the body produces from fatty acids for energy in the absence of dietary carbohydrates. When you enter ketosis (a state of producing ketones), you burn more fat. Growth hormone increases, promoting the burning of fat and the preservation of muscle mass. (You still lose some muscle, just at a slower rate than before.)

I myself have never noticed feeling any different when in ketosis, whether while eating low-carb or while fasting, though I have read accounts of people who say that they do indeed feel different.
